learningObjective: Explain vLLM's PagedAttention design intent: the KV-cache memory-fragmentation problem it targets.

canonicalClaims.claim: PagedAttention (vLLM) targets KV-cache memory inefficiency in transformer inference: when each sequence's KV cache is stored as one contiguous buffer sized to a worst-case sequence length, internal fragmentation (unused reserved slots) and external fragmentation (holes between finished and active sequences) waste GPU memory; PagedAttention stores KV in fixed-size blocks with a page table, enabling near-zero internal waste and better memory utilization.
conditions: Serving multiple concurrent sequences with varying lengths.
GPU HBM is the constrained resource.
The attention kernel supports non-contiguous KV access via a page table.
nonImplications: Does not imply PagedAttention reduces attention compute or FLOPs; the speedup at the system level comes from higher effective batch size on the same GPU, not per-token compute.
Does not imply that PagedAttention's specific throughput numbers generalize to arbitrary hardware; the paper reports measurements on specific GPUs and workloads.

sourceMappings.locator: §3 KV cache fragmentation problem and PagedAttention design

misconceptions.claim: PagedAttention accelerates the attention kernel itself by using paged memory access patterns that improve GPU cache locality.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The primary contribution is memory-management (better KV utilization ⇒ larger effective batch); the paged attention kernel is designed to match, not exceed, contiguous-KV kernel throughput per token.

misconceptions.claim: PagedAttention eliminates KV cache entirely, storing keys and values only when needed via recomputation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: PagedAttention does not eliminate the KV cache; it stores it in paged blocks so that memory is used more efficiently.

misconceptions.claim: PagedAttention's design assumes all sequences have the same length; it does not help when sequence lengths vary widely.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The design specifically targets variable-length sequences; that is where contiguous-KV reservation wastes the most memory.
